resolution_source_risk: If Hits Daily Double chart data is unavailable or partially unavailable by Jun 26, 2026, all affected markets resolve No, regardless of true sales.
rationale: Weekly album chart sales are an aggregate of millions of consumer purchases, not a decision any group makes. The hammer price at a live Sotheby's auction is set by competitive bidding in real time. The auction house knows reserves and pre-sale estimates and registered bidder interest, but no one decides or knows the final price before the gavel falls.
Same structure as other live Sotheby's lots: the final sale price is determined by live bidding in the room, not by any group's advance decision. Estimates are informative but not determinative.

A polling average is an aggregate of many independent survey respondents and polling firms recomputed continuously; there is no small group that already knows the value at a future snapshot time. This is a forecasting question, not a knowledge question.

The exact count of distinct days with a tagged Getty editorial photo over a week is the emergent result of many independent photographers, editors, and news events; no one, including Trump's own staff, controls or knows this count in advance. A classic rate/count question, not an insider-knowledge one.

insider_group: Supreme Court justices and their clerks (post-conference vote, pre-opinion release)
rules_note: Rules require a merits ruling that the TPS termination survives the APA/equal-protection challenges specifically; a dismissal, DIG, or remand without deciding that question resolves No even though it is not literally a ruling 'against' the termination — narrower than a plain reading of the title suggests.
rationale: SCOTUS cases are decided in conference well before the written opinion is released, so a small, named group (the justices and clerks) knows the outcome first. The bucket is moderate rather than strong because it is unclear whether this specific case's conference vote has already occurred as of the close date, and the resolution criterion carves out several non-merits dispositions as No.

insider_group: the administration officials who set and implement tariff policy

insider_group: FIFA/World Cup organizers and the named artists' management and label teams who negotiate and finalize bookings
rules_note: Resolution is on ANNOUNCEMENT of an anticipated performance, not on the performance actually happening — if an announced artist later withdraws, the market still resolves Yes. A naive reader of the title ('who will perform') would expect an actual-performance requirement.
rationale: Halftime-show lineups are booked and contractually finalized by organizers and artist camps well before public announcement, matching the thesis's entertainment-marketing strong case. The rule that resolution triggers on announcement alone (surviving a later withdrawal) makes this an even more mechanical insider-knowledge case than a typical booking market.

Billboard Hot 100 position is an aggregate of streaming and sales behavior across the whole tracking week. The market closes June 29, before the Jul 4 tracking week even begins, so not even industry mid-week trackers have data yet. No group can know the outcome at close.

insider_group: Future's label, A&R, and production team, who finalize the tracklist and its featured artists before release
rationale: Album tracklists and features are typically locked internally by the artist's team well ahead of release, and industry sourcing/leaks are common, giving a plausible informed group. Kept at moderate rather than strong because features can be added, dropped, or renegotiated late in mastering, and there is no confirmation the tracklist is already finalized as of today.

insider_group: Mayor Mamdani's office, which drafts and schedules any executive orders it intends to sign
rules_note: Rules restrict the count to NON-EMERGENCY executive orders, a qualifier absent from the plain title ('above 0 executive orders'), so an emergency order signed in the window would not count toward Yes.
rationale: Signing an executive order is entirely within the mayor's own discretion and staff would know in advance if one is planned/drafted for this window, unlike a market depending on outside actors. Moderate rather than strong because there is no specific evidence any order is currently planned for this particular week.
